result.summary: Independently re-verified REQ-029 (QR check-in via ci_ deep link; GitHub issue #32; depends_on REQ-028; second requirement of Phase 6) at commit d09fd06, branch feature/WF02-REQ-029. Did not trust TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 report, the test report yaml, or any prior gate's summary as a substitute for my own re-derivation. 1. Read docs/agents/design/REQ-029.md in full (all 12 sections, AC1-AC7) then read the shipped diff directly (git diff master...HEAD --stat: 23 files, 3360 insertions/9 deletions -- domain/event.ts's StartPayload 'checkin' branch, domain/registration.ts's new getRegistrationByQrTokenForCheckin/getCheckinActorDisplayName/getRegistrationDisplayInfo/decideQrCheckinOutcome/performQrCheckIn/decideOverrideOutcome/overrideAdmitAndCheckIn plus exporting deriveCheckinDisplayName, domain/eventStaffAuthorization.ts's two-function additive extension, handlers/checkinQr.ts (new), handlers/start.ts's second dispatch branch, i18n en/ru/types' new checkinQr.* keys, index.ts's new callback registration, plus the design doc, test spec, and this run's own handoffs/test-report). Confirmed the diff matches the design line-for-line: §2.1's SELECT structurally excludes profiles.phone/profiles.email; §3.2's decideQrCheckinOutcome and §4.1's decideOverrideOutcome are the exact first-match-wins tables stated in the design; §3.3's performQrCheckIn opens one transaction, does a FOR UPDATE fresh read, performs the S4 token-currency recheck (`row.qrToken !== qrToken` -> treated as unknown-token) BEFORE calling decideQrCheckinOutcome, and writes at most one UPDATE + one writeAuditLog call on the check-in branch only (no write on refused-not-admitted or already-checked-in); §4.2's overrideAdmitAndCheckIn performs exactly one UPDATE (admission+check-in fields together) and exactly one writeAuditLog call; §5's extended requireEventStaffForEvent/buildCheckinRefusalAudit add one optional trailing registrationId parameter each, defaulting to today's exact behavior when omitted. Directly confirmed via `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/domain/eventStaffAuthorization.ts` that the change is purely additive: buildCheckinRefusalAudit gains `registrationId?: string`, and its entity/entityId selection becomes `registrationId === undefined ? 'event'/eventId : 'registration'/registrationId` -- every REQ-018/028 call site (which omits the new parameter) is byte-for-byte unaffected, and only REQ-029's own call site (checkinQr.ts's resolveCheckinQrDeepLink) supplies it. 2. Re-ran npm run lint myself: 0 errors, the same 2 pre-existing apps/web LCP warnings (Footer.tsx, Nav.tsx) unrelated to this diff -- matches TEST-RUNNER exactly. Re-ran npm run build myself: apps/web (Next.js/Turbopack) and apps/bot (tsc) both clean. Stood up my own scratch Postgres (apps/bot/docker-compose.yml, port 55432; container did not exist yet in this session -- `docker compose up -d` created and started it fresh), ran `DATABASE_URL=... npx drizzle-kit migrate` myself (applied cleanly), then `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` from the repo root: 29 files / 293 tests passed, 0 failed -- matches TEST-RUNNER's reported count exactly (293/293). 3. Independent re-verification with my own fresh fixtures (apps/bot/scratch-rv-req029.ts and apps/bot/scratch-rv-req029-crossflow.ts -- written, run, then deleted; git status confirmed clean before and after both), calling the domain functions directly, never reusing BACKEND-DEV's/TEST-RUNNER's committed test files' exact fixtures, tgId bands, or event/chapter data (own tgId bands 995000001+/996000001+, own chapters/events): - AC1 (non-staff scan refused + audit row naming the registration): seeded Event X and Event Y under the same chapter, made a distinct user real EventStaff of Event Y ONLY (not X), had an attendee admitted to Event X. Called requireEventStaffForEvent directly with Event Y-staff's tgId against Event X's registration/eventId/registrationId. Result: authResult.ok === false, reason === 'not-staff-for-event'; exactly one new checkin.refused audit_log row with entity==='registration', entityId===the attendee's registrationId (not either event's id), actorUserId===the cross-event staffer's own users.id; the registration's checked_in_at remained null -- AC1 independently reproduced, PASS. - eventStaffAuthorization.ts backward-compatibility (4th independent confirmation across the pipeline, given this is the highest-risk shared-module change): called buildCheckinRefusalAudit(null, eventId, 'no-user') with the new registrationId parameter OMITTED -- confirmed entity stays 'event' and entityId stays eventId, exactly REQ-018/028's original behavior, unchanged -- PASS. - AC2 (repeat-scan zero-write proof): built my own admitted registration and staff fixture, called performQrCheckIn directly for the first scan (outcome.kind==='check-in'), captured Postgres's own hidden xmin system column immediately after via a raw SQL query, then called performQrCheckIn again with the SAME token (outcome.kind==='already-checked-in'), captured xmin again. Result: xmin identical across the two reads (a strictly stronger proof than 'the values didn't change' -- it proves no UPDATE touched the row's storage tuple at all, the same standard TEST-RUNNER's own report used), checked_in_at byte-for-byte identical, still exactly one registration.checkin audit row after the second scan -- AC2 independently reproduced with my own fixture and my own direct raw-SQL xmin capture (not reusing the committed test file's helper), PASS. 4. Cross-flow (manual REQ-028 <-> QR REQ-029) coherence sanity check, requested by task step 6, verified empirically with a dedicated scratch script rather than by code-reading alone: - Scenario A: registered an attendee, manually checked them in via toggleCheckIn (REQ-028) -- registrations row got check_in_method='manual', checked_in_at set. Then scanned the SAME attendee's qr_token through performQrCheckIn (REQ-029). Result: outcome.kind==='already-checked-in' (not a fresh check-in), check_in_method remained 'manual' (QR path did not overwrite it), checked_in_at unchanged across the scan, and getCheckinActorDisplayName correctly resolved the manual-checking staff member's display name for the report -- confirming REQ-029's QR path correctly reads and reports a REQ-028 manual check-in without double-writing. - Scenario B: registered a second attendee, checked them in via performQrCheckIn (REQ-029) -- check_in_method='qr'. Then called toggleCheckIn (REQ-028's manual list toggle) against the same registration. Result: toggleCheckIn read decideCheckinToggleOutcome's input purely from checked_in_at (never check_in_method) and correctly returned 'undo' (since checked_in_at was non-null), clearing checked_in_at -- confirming REQ-028's manual list correctly recognizes and can toggle off a REQ-029 QR check-in. Both directions confirm the two flows share and interpret checked_in_at/checked_in_by/check_in_method consistently, exactly as the design's shared-schema section (REQ-029 §0, reusing REQ-028's untouched checked_in_at/checked_in_by/check_in_method columns and CHECK constraint) requires. No coherence gap found. 5. Confirmed full requirement scope: git diff --stat lists only design-doc-listed files (domain/event.ts, domain/eventStaffAuthorization.ts, domain/registration.ts, handlers/checkinQr.ts (new) + its two committed test files, handlers/start.ts, i18n/en.ts+ru.ts+types.ts, index.ts, the design doc, the test spec, and this run's own handoffs/test-report) -- nothing stray. git grep -in 'TODO\|FIXME\|XXX' across the touched source files (registration.ts, eventStaffAuthorization.ts, checkinQr.ts, start.ts, event.ts, i18n files, index.ts): zero matches. git status --porcelain clean before and after this handoff (both my scratch scripts removed after use). Schema: confirmed no migration files were added in this diff (git diff --stat shows no apps/bot/drizzle/*.sql entries) -- matches the design's §0 'no change needed' conclusion, and matches this run's own db/schema.ts having zero diff. 6. docs/agents/requirements.yaml staleness check: REQ-029's entry (line 1478) still reads status: pending, which is correct and NOT stale at this point in the pipeline -- DOC-UPDATER (Step 6, which has not yet run) is the step that flips it to done. No other staleness found relative to what actually shipped (title/description match the shipped scope; depends_on: [REQ-028] is satisfied, REQ-028 already done). 7. Filed-issue judgment: confirmed via `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/handlers/staff.ts` returning EMPTY that ISS-0020 (MAJOR, REQ-018's staff.ts assignment-notification blocked-user gap) is genuinely untouched by this diff and correctly out of scope, as the task context states. ISS-0013 (MAJOR, CI has no Postgres service) is a pre-existing CI-infrastructure gap unrelated to this requirement's own surface -- does not block a release-validation gate that itself independently stood up and ran the DB-backed suite outside CI. ISS-0014, ISS-0015-0019, ISS-0021-0024 (all MINOR, test-spec documentation-precision issues for other, already-shipped requirements) and ISS-0025 (MINOR, REQ-028's own test-spec worked-example issue, already assessed non-blocking in REQ-028's own release validation) are unrelated to REQ-029's surface. No new issue was filed against REQ-029 itself by any gate in this run (TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's issues: [] confirmed by direct read; TEST-RUNNER's issues: [] confirmed by direct read). None of the filed issues should block this release. Overall: every independent check -- lint, build, the full 293-test suite from the repo root (freshly stood-up scratch Postgres), my own AC1 fixture using a genuinely distinct cross-event-staff scenario, my own direct backward-compatibility call to buildCheckinRefusalAudit with the new parameter omitted, my own AC2 fixture with an independent raw-SQL xmin capture, my own two-scenario cross-flow (manual<->QR) empirical proof, confirmation that domain/staff.ts has literally zero diff -- agrees with all prior gates (CODE-DESIGNER/VALIDATOR, BACKEND-DEV, REVIEWER, SECURITY-REVIEWER, TEST-DESIGNER/VALIDATOR, TEST-RUNNER). No half-implemented scope, no stray TODOs, clean git tree, all design-doc-listed files present, no schema/migration changes. Manual (REQ-028) and QR (REQ-029) check-in flows are coherent: both read and write the same checked_in_at/checked_in_by/check_in_method fields with no double-write or divergent-interpretation gap in either direction.
